# Auto-instrumentation for AI agents

Auto-instrumentation generates OpenTelemetry spans for AI model calls and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls without any tracing code in your applications. The [AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access) and the [MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access) combine Envoy with a protocol-aware processor that reads each call as it passes through. Applications need no tracing SDK, manual spans, or decorators. This approach is sometimes called zero-code instrumentation.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To set it up, refer to [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

Network telemetry shows which services talked and whether requests succeeded. AI workflows also need the content of each exchange: which tool an agent called, with what arguments, and what came back. That detail travels inside application protocols, not in network span attributes.

The proxies read those protocols as traffic passes through them:

- The AI Inference Gateway instruments supported model requests and responses.
- MCP Sidecars instrument supported tool calls, including the tool name, arguments, results, and errors, subject to your content-capture policy.

For example, an agent can call the same tool with the same arguments many times while every HTTP request succeeds. The proxy spans record each call and its result, so Agentic Analytics can detect the repetition for [cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) without custom spans in the application.

Auto-instrumentation covers only traffic that passes through these proxies. Calls that bypass the mesh and tools that run inside the agent process are not instrumented. Refer to [Limitations](#limitations).

Some details on this page come from the reference deployment, an example deployment of these components. They are labeled as such, and your deployment can differ.

## How auto-instrumentation works

Each proxy produces two kinds of spans, and trace context ties them into one workflow trace.

The following diagram shows one request through a proxy and the spans it produces. Solid arrows are requests. Dotted arrows point to the span each part emits. Both spans are children of the entry span.

![A request passes from the agent through Envoy to the model or tool, while Envoy emits an egress span and the external processor emits a payload span, both children of the entry span.](/img/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation-spans_light.png#light-theme-only)
![A request passes from the agent through Envoy to the model or tool, while Envoy emits an egress span and the external processor emits a payload span, both children of the entry span.](/img/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation-spans_dark.png#dark-theme-only)

Envoy and the processor each emit a span. Both spans take their parent from the incoming `traceparent` header, so they appear as siblings under the entry span.

### Network spans

Envoy generates network spans for observed ingress and egress requests. They describe the service path, request timing, and transport outcome.

Network observation needs HTTP-aware listeners. Opaque TCP forwarding does not expose the HTTP headers and bodies that payload observation reads.

### Payload spans

The external processor runs next to Envoy and receives request and response headers and bodies through Envoy's `ext_proc` interface. It parses supported protocols and emits a payload span for each AI interaction it observes. The processor is infrastructure, not a library that the agent or tool imports.

In the reference deployment, the processor returns the payload unmodified and exports spans through a bounded background queue after the exchange, so the application does not wait for trace storage.

The payload span is a separate span, not extra attributes on Envoy's span. External processing runs before the router creates the egress span, so the two spans share a parent and appear as siblings.

### Payload span sensitive data security

<Warning>

Payload spans can contain prompts, completions, tool arguments, tool results, and delegation messages. Auto-instrumentation does not redact them. Filter or redact sensitive data before it reaches telemetry storage or analytics destinations.

</Warning>

Follow these guidelines to protect sensitive data:

- Do not turn on content capture for a workload when the deployed path cannot filter or redact it.
- Keep credentials, tokens, and personal data out of telemetry.
- Restrict access to and retention of the remaining evidence.
- Expect redaction to limit downstream analysis, including cycle detection.
- Do not use trace IDs, arguments, prompts, or results as metric labels.

### Trace context propagation

The proxies correlate observations with the [W3C Trace Context specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). Establish the trace context and a sampling decision once, at the entry point, so that every component on the request path receives the same value. In the reference deployment, an infrastructure trace-root component in front of the API gateway does this.

The sampling decision travels as the sampled flag, the lowest bit of the `trace-flags` field in the `traceparent` header. A `trace-flags` value of `01` means sampled, and `00` means not sampled.

Applications must forward the incoming context on their downstream calls. The reference applications forward `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`, and `x-request-id`. Forwarding headers is not instrumentation, so applications still create no spans.

A proxy cannot tell which incoming request caused an outgoing request inside an application. Without propagation, observations do not join into one workflow trace. In the reference deployment, a missing, invalid, or unsampled `traceparent` stops the processor from emitting a payload span.

## Observed signals

The following table lists what the proxies observe for each type of interaction. What's available depends on the protocol, the visible request and response data, sampling, and size limits.

| Interaction | Observed evidence |
| --- | --- |
| MCP tool call | JSON-RPC method, tool name, arguments, result text, and protocol or tool errors |
| Model inference | Model identifier, visible prompt and completion content, offered tools, requested tool calls, and usage fields in the response |
| Agent-to-agent delegation | Supported Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol method and message content |
| Supported HTTP API call | Request method and path, response status, and supported JSON payload information |
| Mesh request | Service path, network timing, and transport outcome |

MCP payload spans use attributes such as `mcp.tool`, `mcp.arguments`, `mcp.result.text`, and `mcp.is_error`. Inference payload spans use `gen_ai.*` attributes. The schema is version specific, and not every attribute is available for every provider or protocol version.

A tool call requested in a model response does not mean the agent ran the tool. Match it to the actual tool request. To turn these signals into metrics and KPIs, refer to [Operational metrics](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability#operational-metrics).

## Telemetry pipeline

The following components carry spans from the proxies to analysis. For where they sit in a full deployment, refer to the [architecture overview](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture).

| Component | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Entry point | Establishes or preserves trace context and the sampling decision |
| AI Inference Gateway | Instruments supported model exchanges |
| MCP Sidecar | Instruments supported tool exchanges |
| Envoy | Generates network spans and passes supported exchanges to the external processor |
| External processor | Parses visible protocol data and generates correlated payload spans |
| OpenTelemetry Collector | Receives spans and exports them to configured destinations |
| Trace backend | Stores spans and makes traces queryable |
| Span relay | Extracts trace IDs and queues analysis jobs when analytics is enabled |
| Agentic Analytics | Retrieves traces and evaluates workflow behavior, including unproductive repetition |

In the reference deployment, Envoy sends spans to the collector over OTLP gRPC on port `4317`, and the processor sends spans over OTLP HTTP at `/v1/traces` on port `4318`. The collector exports spans to Tempo and can send a copy to the span relay. The relay queues trace IDs, not payloads, on a BullMQ queue, and analytics workers use the IDs to retrieve each trace from storage.

## Limitations

- **Coverage.** Proxies observe only traffic that passes through them with readable HTTP content. They do not observe TLS passed through as opaque traffic, calls that bypass the mesh, tools that run inside the agent, or operations inside an external provider.
- **Protocol support.** The processor must understand the protocol. Unsupported or opaque payloads produce network spans only.
- **Body size.** Buffering bodies adds work to the request path and imposes size limits. Envoy can reject an oversized request before the processor sees it, and fail-open external processing does not bypass Envoy's buffer limits. Align listener buffers, processor gRPC limits, exporter capacity, and storage limits.
- **Streaming.** Buffered JSON observation does not guarantee support for incremental streaming. Test streaming behavior separately.
- **Incomplete evidence.** Sampling, truncation, missing context, and delivery loss produce incomplete traces. The reference parsers mark truncated attributes. Do not compare truncated arguments or results as if they were complete.
- **Double counting.** One logical call can produce network, payload, and external-processing transport spans, and a gateway can observe the same model exchange on both sides. Do not count every span as a separate call or billable event. External processing observes the logical exchange, not each Envoy retry.
- **Delivery.** A collector acknowledgment does not prove that every destination stored the span. Monitor processor stream counts, skipped spans, export failures, dropped spans, collector queue failures, and backend availability.
- **Scope.** Traces do not reveal private model reasoning, prove task completion, measure model quality, or replace authorization. Trace storage is not an audit ledger or a billing system.
